note: 500 files x 1,000 cases (00-FF minus 11 holes and CB, plus CB 00-FF), per-M-cycle bus samples; generated by JSMoo's SM83 core, which its README says was 'created by translating Ares' SM83 core'. Emulator-derived. 107 MB.
v2: 242 files, 100 cases per opcode (CB 25,600), TomHarte format, decode-execute-prefetch; generator not stated (provenance unknown). v1 (474 MB, deprecated) not fetched.
sources; built ROMs come from the pinned zip (reference/roms/). Each test's header lists the models it was verified on; README lists the device fleet.
blargg's Game Boy test ROMs (cpu_instrs, instr_timing, mem_timing, mem_timing-2, halt_bug, interrupt_time, oam_bug, dmg_sound, cgb_sound) with sources; 2015 mirror.

test/hwtests: 3,524 .asm tests whose expected screen output was captured on DMG (dmg08) and CGB (cgb04c) hardware, encoded in each filename; test/qdgbas.py assembles them. Upstream sinamas/gambatte is now private (its GitHub repo is a README only).
LIJI's hardware-research tests (APU, DMA, interrupts incl. ei_delay_halt).
Core/sm83_cpu.c is the most explicit emulator CPU; Tester/ builds a headless runner; BootROMs/ builds free boot ROMs (needs rgbds).
Game Boy: Complete Technical Reference, Typst source; chapter/cpu/instruction-set.typ has per-M-cycle addr/data/IDU/ALU tables for every instruction except HALT, STOP, DAA (TODO in source).
dmgops.json: per-opcode lengths, T-cycles, flags and per-M-cycle access type.
Opcodes.json: mnemonic, bytes, cycles, operands, flags; the input for generating an opcode table.
Game Boy Instruction Tester: compares a CPU against a bundled reference implementation instruction by instruction (emulator-derived).
GateBoy/LogicBoy. README: the CPU is NOT from the die ('GateBoy's CPU is instead my current best guess'); gate-level for the rest of the DMG only.

SystemVerilog generated from msinger/dmg-schematics netlists of a DMG-CPU B die, INCLUDING the SM83 core (sm83/sm83.sv and its decoders). Icarus Verilog. tests/ holds expected results (blargg, mooneye) and xfail lists; boot/quickboot.bin is a free fast boot ROM.
